text.en: Asha folded a paper to make a triangle and then a rectangle. "Shapes follow rules," said her teacher.

Two lines cut by a transversal make pairs of angles: corresponding, alternate and co-interior. The angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees and its exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Congruent triangles are of the same shape and size and are proved by the SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS rules.
A quadrilateral has four sides, and its angles add up to 360 degrees. Special types are the parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezium and kite. In a parallelogram, opposite sides and opposite angles are equal and the diagonals bisect each other.
A circle has parts such as the centre, radius, chord, diameter, arc and segment. The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord, equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre, and a cyclic quadrilateral has opposite angles that add up to 180 degrees. Practical geometry constructs these figures with a ruler and compass.

problem.en: Two angles of a triangle are 50 and 60 degrees. Find the third.

prompt.en: A friend says The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 180 degrees. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: A triangle's angles add up to 180.

points.en: Perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord.
Cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles sum to 180.
